With maturity, there comes a more refined realization that you don't possess the individual power to shape the world on your own. Sometimes things start to head in a direction that you don't want, but what other option do you have? You either ride the wave or get pummeled in its wake.

Bruce Lee had a quote, "Be like water, friend." By this, he meant that those who are fluid and malleable can endure some of the harshest circumstances and shift shapes to deal with it. By contrast, those who are rigid like stone are crushed when faced with the same circumstances.

I guess this leads me to two conclusions which are a duality of sorts. 1) Be flexible in the face of adversity and able to change depending on what is required of you in these new times. But, this leads to point, 2) Don't just be a pushover and become spiritually defeated when the time comes for change. Just because you are 'flexible' doesn't mean you should lose all of your principles or values. A median can be found where you can hold onto your core values while not being so anchored down by them that you are crushed by the incoming current.
